source: The 14 steps and checklists are condensed from The Startup Blueprint: 14 Steps to Building Your Dream Business (2nd ed., 2025) by Derick van Vuren.

gates.name: Worth testing
gates.spend: Research only: customer interviews, a survey tool, the simulated panel. No product, no lease, no inventory.
gates.question: Is this a real opportunity, for this founder, that survives a pre-mortem?

gates.name: Worth a real-world test
gates.spend: A small test budget: a landing page, a pop-up, a pre-order page, a few paid ads. Nothing you cannot afford to lose.
gates.question: Do we know who buys, why, and where the gap is?

gates.name: Worth building
gates.spend: The startup budget: equipment, build-out, inventory, product development.
gates.question: Does every unit make money, does year 1 work, and did real buyers confirm it?

gates.name: Ready to launch and grow
gates.spend: Launch, legal registration, trademarks, hiring, growth spend.
gates.question: Is the company set up, the sales engine ready, the cash sufficient and the team planned?

steps.title: The Idea
steps.question: Is this an idea or an opportunity?

items.text: Write a one-paragraph problem statement: the problem, who has it, how often, how badly
Validate the problem in conversations with 10 or more potential customers (not friends or family)
Document the pain points and the solutions customers use today
Decide whether it is a must-have or a nice-to-have, with the evidence
Name the trends or changes that make now the right time
List your key assumptions about the market and the customers
Write a first vision statement for the venture

steps.title: The Entrepreneur
steps.question: Are you the right founder for this, and are you ready?

items.text: Complete the founder profile: entrepreneur type, strengths and weaknesses
List the skills this business needs and mark the gaps
Plan each gap: learn it, partner for it, or hire it
Find at least one mentor in this industry
Confirm your family or partner supports the plan
Know your personal runway: months of living costs covered
Set boundaries between personal and business life, and a plan for stress

steps.title: Prepare to Reach Success: Mind Games
steps.question: Have outsiders tested your thinking, and do you know when you would stop?

items.text: Name the two or three biases most likely to fool you, each with a countermeasure
Run a pre-mortem: the board and the red team
Write kill criteria before any test: the results that mean stop or pivot
Set SMART goals and quarterly milestones
Choose the KPIs you will review every month
Set up accountability: a mentor, peer or advisor you report to every month

steps.title: Laying the Foundation: Legal Form, Naming and Branding
steps.question: Is the company set up properly, and is the name yours to use?

items.text: Shortlist names and run the free checks: trademark register, domain, social handles
Choose the legal structure with an accountant or lawyer in your country
Register the business and the name (after Gate 3)
Open a business bank account and set up bookkeeping
Get the licenses, permits and insurance this business needs
Basic brand: logo, colors, a simple website or landing page, consistent messaging
Basic contracts, terms, and a privacy policy if you collect customer data

steps.title: Create Your Value Proposition
steps.question: Why should someone buy from you?

items.text: Complete the Value Proposition Canvas: jobs, pains, gains, and how you relieve and create them
Write the value proposition statement in one sentence you can say from memory
Test the statement with real target customers and refine it
Check it is clear, relevant, unique and credible

steps.title: Find Your Customers
steps.question: Who exactly buys, and have you heard it from them?

items.text: Hold 20 or more customer interviews about past behavior, not opinions
Build a customer avatar from the research, one per major segment
Map the customer journey from awareness to purchase
Estimate TAM, SAM and SOM with the sources
Collect a demand signal: a waitlist, signups, deposits or pre-sales
Decide how you will keep customers: onboarding, support, loyalty

steps.title: Do Market Segmentation
steps.question: Which segment do you serve first?

items.text: Segment the market: demographic, psychographic, behavioral and needs-based (firmographic for B2B)
Check each segment is measurable, accessible, substantial, actionable and distinct
Choose ONE primary segment to start with, and say why
Write the message for the primary segment

steps.title: Understand Competition Using Porter's 5 Forces
steps.question: Is the industry attractive, and where is the gap?

items.text: Identify the top 3 to 5 direct competitors and the indirect ones and substitutes
Rate all five forces with evidence
Write a strategic response to every high force
Set up competitor monitoring (alerts, a monthly check of prices and reviews)

steps.title: Determine Your Price
steps.question: Is the price set on purpose, and will buyers pay it?

items.text: Choose the positioning strategy and the pricing method (never a random guess)
Research competitor prices for the same job, like for like
Know the lowest price that still covers each unit's cost
Test price sensitivity with real buyers (two prices, a pre-sale, a survey)
Plan how the price evolves as you add features or scale

steps.title: Know Your Value Chain
steps.question: Can you deliver the promise at a profit, every time?

items.text: Map the primary and support activities
Cost every activity and name the value it creates
Decide what to strengthen, optimize, outsource or cut
Get real quotes for the main inputs from at least two suppliers

steps.title: Design Your Business Model and Write Your Business Plan
steps.question: Do the numbers work, and did real buyers confirm the model?

items.text: Fill in all nine blocks of the Business Model Canvas
Test the riskiest assumption with real customers (the real-world test)
Build the financial model: year 1 by month, break-even, cash needed
Know CAC, lifetime value and payback
Run best, expected and worst cases
Write the lean plan (1 to 2 pages) and the full plan

steps.title: Sell Your Product
steps.question: Is there a repeatable way to turn strangers into customers?

items.text: Define the sales funnel: awareness, interest, decision, purchase, loyalty
Pick one or two channels where the primary segment spends attention
Write the sales script and the objection answers
Set up tracking: leads, conversion, cost per customer (a spreadsheet is fine)
Plan the launch campaign with dates
Test products, systems and support before launch day

steps.title: Grow Your Business: Bootstrap, Game Theory, Scaling
steps.question: Is there enough cash, and a plan for how to grow?

items.text: Choose the funding path: bootstrap, friends and family, loan, angels or venture capital
Know your burn rate and runway, and review them monthly
Map how the main competitor will react to your launch and your price (a game tree)
Decide whether you are growing (costs rise with revenue) or scaling (they do not)
Document the key processes so someone else could run them

steps.title: Build Your Team
steps.question: Who do you need, when, and how will you pay them?

items.text: Define the first roles that complement your skills (technical, growth, operations)
Write the company values before the first hire
Set the compensation approach, including any equity
Plan a structured interview process and onboarding
Plan the team for the next 12 to 24 months
